subject: math
cluster: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles

items.prompt:
Sine is defined as:
A) $\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$
B) $\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$
C) $\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$
D) $\frac{\text{hypotenuse}}{\text{opposite}}$

Cosine is defined as:
A) $\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$
B) $\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$
C) $\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$
D) $\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{opposite}}$

Tangent is defined as:
A) $\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$
B) $\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$
C) $\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$
D) $\frac{\text{hypotenuse}}{\text{opposite}}$

Opposite $3$, hypotenuse $5$. Then $\sin$ is:
A) $\frac{3}{4}$
B) $\frac{3}{5}$
C) $\frac{4}{5}$
D) $\frac{5}{3}$

Adjacent $4$, hypotenuse $5$. Then $\cos$ is:
A) $\frac{3}{5}$
B) $\frac{4}{5}$
C) $\frac{4}{3}$
D) $\frac{5}{4}$

Opposite $3$, adjacent $4$. Then $\tan$ is:
A) $\frac{3}{5}$
B) $\frac{4}{5}$
C) $\frac{3}{4}$
D) $\frac{4}{3}$

Why do trig ratios depend only on the angle?
A) Triangles are congruent
B) Same-angle right triangles are similar, so side ratios are equal
C) Sides are always equal
D) They do not
items.answer: B) Same-angle right triangles are similar, so side ratios are equal

steps: Similar triangles share equal side ratios.

items.prompt:
In a right triangle, opposite $8$ and hypotenuse $10$. Then $\sin$ simplifies to:
A) $\frac{4}{5}$
B) $\frac{8}{10}$ only
C) $\frac{3}{5}$
D) $\frac{5}{4}$
